newsitem.title: UK: Delayed Egypt raw sugar arrivals expected from June.
newsitem.headline: Delayed Egypt raw sugar arrivals expected from June.

text.p: Egypt should be taking delivery of several cargoes of raw sugar in the next month or so after it requested international suppliers to delay shipments, physical traders said on Friday.

Egypt is thought to have contracted some 750,000 tonnes for its 1997 delivery programme but in March asked for deferment to June/July due to weak internal prices and fears of developing congestion at Alexandria.
Traders said the deferment could apply to as much as 100,000 tonnes of raws, depending on the contractual penalty agreed upon and the agreement of the suppliers.
"I imagine some of those will be arriving soon...but they probably had to pay up for the deferment," said one.
Much of the raws would be Cuban in origin although more north Brazil sugar was now likely to be included after being substituted on account of expected scarcity of Cuban cargoes after June.
Traders said Egypt was unlikely to buy any more sugar for the present and would wait for its contracted deliveries to arrive in the second half.
"Egypt won't pick up any spot/prompts unless they're bargains and you'd be better off selling into the Black Sea right now," said another trader.
Egypt's sugar imports mainly come from Cuba and Brazil. It also takes smaller quantities from the European Union.
According to data from the International Sugar Organization (ISO), its imports totalled 1.08 million tonnes in 1995, almost double the amount for 1994.
Egypt plans to become self-sufficient in sugar with a programme of expanded beet production and reduced imports of raw sugar.
